title: Power Apps: modern, refreshed look reaches embedded model-driven apps on the semiannual channel
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing requirement, environment setting and API are supported. Two minor corrections remain: cite the documentation about unchanged data and permissions, and remove the checklist instruction to inspect app and user overrides because those controls have no table rows.

claims.claim: This roadmap change is for Power Apps.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Apps"]

claims.claim: The modern look extends to embedded model-driven app experiences, retaining consistent Fluent styling and interaction patterns inside another host.
claims.quote: Extends the modern, refreshed look to embedded app experiences so model-driven app content retains consistent Fluent styling and interaction patterns when it appears inside another host.

claims.claim: At the time of writing, Learn does not describe the embedded experience under that name or identify its hosts.

claims.claim: Learn says navigation supports only SVG custom icons with the modern look.
claims.quote: Only SVG icons are supported. If you use other formats such as PNG, the navigation doesn't display them and a default icon appears instead.

claims.claim: Model-driven apps are premium apps by default.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default.

claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps embedded model-driven modern refreshed look specific license price meter. Opened powerapps-licensing-faq and modern-fluent-design; read licensing overview search excerpt. No refresh-specific license found.

claims.claim: The FAQ points to the Power Platform Licensing Guide for the full list of qualifying licenses.
claims.quote: For the complete and current list of qualifying licenses that provide premium Power Apps use rights, refer to the Microsoft Power Platform Licensing Guide.

claims.claim: The semiannual channel turns on GA-ready features in April and October.
claims.quote: The semi-annual channel turns on generally available (GA) ready features twice a year, in April and October.

claims.claim: The semiannual build follows gradual weekly rollout, so environments receive it on different dates.
claims.quote: Because builds roll out to the region groups over successive weekends, the date an environment receives a given build depends on its region group.

claims.claim: Channel checks run in order: URL override, user override, non-Auto app channel, then non-Auto environment channel.
claims.quote:
1. URL override.
2. User channel override.
3. App release channel value other than Auto (for example, Monthly, Semi-annual).
4. Environment release channel value other than Auto (for example, Monthly, Semi-annual).

claims.claim: The environment channel control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Behavior > Release channel > Model-driven app release channel.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Behavior.
## Release channel
| Model-driven app release channel |

claims.claim: PATCH /organizations(<organizationid>) updates the organization record used for the environment channel setting.
claims.quote: | `Update`Event: True | `PATCH` /organizations(*organizationid*)See [Update]

claims.claim: Changing the environment behavior setting requires the System Administrator role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: The request body sets the organization's releasechannel property to change the environment release channel.
claims.quote: Developers can change the environment channel by updating the ReleaseChannel column value for the row in the Organization table.

claims.claim: The releasechannel value 3 means Semi-annual channel.
claims.quote: LogicalName | `releasechannel` ... ReleaseChannel Choices/Options ... | 3 | **Semi-annual channel** |

claims.claim: The release channel controls when model-driven app features arrive rather than acting as a switch specific to this look.
claims.quote: You can control how often the users in your organization get these new features by specifying the release channel. ... The release channel settings described in this article apply to model-driven apps.

claims.claim: The channel-change page says Power Platform model-driven apps with app channel Auto use Monthly regardless of the environment channel.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps in Power Platform environments use Monthly when the app release channel is Auto regardless of the environment release channel. All model-driven apps in Power Platform environments need to set the app release channel explicitly.

claims.claim: Makers can set the app release channel in the app designer or Solutions area.
claims.quote: Use the app channel to override the release channel for a model-driven app by using Power Apps app designer or the Solutions area.

claims.claim: The modern-look page says admins can turn off the New Look using the New look for model driven apps setting.
claims.quote: Admins can turn off the New Look for all users by updating the New look for model driven apps app setting.

claims.claim: The app settings page says the New Look setting is hidden and ignored when the New Look becomes mandatory.
claims.quote: This setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release when the new look becomes mandatory.

claims.claim: Neither cited settings page specifies whether that New Look setting governs the roadmap's embedded app experiences.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps embedded model-driven apps modern refreshed look disable New look setting host. Opened modern-fluent-design and app-properties in full; neither specifies this setting's coverage of the roadmap's embedded app experiences.

claims.claim: Learn says the modern-look change does not affect data or permissions.
claims.quote: There is no impact on app logic, data, or permissions.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/important-changes-coming#deprecation-of-the-classic-look-for-model-driven-apps to sources for the risk rationale's statement that Learn says the modern look does not change data or permissions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to inspect appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Check whether any app or user in those environments overrides the environment channel; see the note under the table for the order Learn gives. The controls table contains only the environment release channel.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Check whether any app or user in those environments overrides the environment channel'; the app and user override checks have no corresponding controls-table rows. Retain the explanatory qualifications below the table.
